Cluster-robust gene screen for Negative-Binomial expert effects

Source: R/score_screen.R
vcmoe_gene_screen.Rd

Screens candidate covariates (typically genes) for an association with the response inside the latent components, while the fitted VCMoE (the null model) is held fixed. For each candidate, every grid point of the null fit is augmented by the covariate, entering each expert's local linear predictor (the tested coefficients) and each gating contrast (nuisance), with coefficients starting at zero. A one-step estimate of the expert coefficients is studentized with the CR2 cluster-robust covariance and calibrated over the grid by a studentized wild cluster bootstrap, as in the path tests of vcmoe_confband(). The null model is fitted once, so all candidates share its moments and the screen scales to thousands of genes.

Usage

vcmoe_gene_screen(
  fit,
  X,
  cluster,
  profile_genes = NULL,
  grids = NULL,
  B = 9999L,
  seed = NULL,
  adjust = c("BH", "minP", "both"),
  chunk_size = 200L,
  control = list(),
  profile_control = list()
)

Arguments

fit

The null model: a single-response Negative-Binomial local-grid vcmoe fit that retains its data.

X

Numeric matrix of candidate covariates, one row per retained fitted row (in fitted-row order) and one uniquely named column per candidate. Columns are centred internally.

cluster

Independent-cluster identifiers (for example donors), one per retained fitted row. Required.

profile_genes

Optional column names of X to screen after profiling their gating effect: the candidate first enters the gating of the null model and every screened grid point is refitted by local EM, giving the restricted local fit under the null (no expert effect, gating effect free). Use this for strong markers of the latent components, whose gating effect is far from zero; the one-step screen holds it at zero.

grids

Grid indices that form the tested path. Defaults to every grid point. A candidate is reported with an NA p-value when any of these grid points is blocked for it.

B

Number of wild bootstrap draws (Webb weights). One set of weights is generated per call and shared by every candidate, chunk and profiled refit, including when seed = NULL. When 6^G <= B for G clusters, all 6^G weight vectors are used.

seed

Optional seed for the bootstrap weights.

adjust

Multiplicity adjustment over the full candidate set: "BH" (Benjamini-Hochberg, default), "minP" (single-step Westfall-Young min-p from the shared draws) or "both". Candidates with an NA p-value stay in the family size of the BH adjustment.

chunk_size

Number of candidates processed together; smaller values use less memory and do not change the results.

control

Optional inference controls passed to the local moment computations (for example strict, max_hessian_dim).

profile_control

List with maxit (default 300) and tol (default 1e-9) for the profiled refits.

Value

A list of class vcmoe_gene_screen with genes (one row per candidate: sup-t statistic, raw and adjusted p-values, maximising component and grid, per-component statistics and directions, per-SD effects, grid usage and status), pointwise (per grid and coefficient one-step estimates, standard errors and Bell-McCaffrey degrees of freedom), grids (grid-level status), profile (profiled refits), draws (shared bootstrap maxima) and settings.

Details

The screen tests expert effects, so the null model should explain component membership well: include covariates that distinguish the latent components (for example known subtype markers) in its gating formula. Otherwise strong markers can leak into the expert test. Results describe associations on the log-mean scale of each expert; effect_per_sd gives the one-step level coefficient at the maximising grid point per standard deviation of the candidate.
